name: Firelight
desc: A fire you never see, doing what firelight actually does to a room — a warm wash spills in from off-frame and falls off toward deep red, unseen things standing between the flame and the scene throw soft wedges of shadow that swing and lengthen as the fire's centroid wanders, the penumbrae going softer the further they travel, and the whole room breathes and gutters gently (never flickers — the strobe band is deliberately empty).

energy.doc: how big the fire is — output, throw, shadow depth and the amplitude of the gutter (capped well below any strobe band)

scale.doc: throw radius vs design size — 0.4 is a match, 2.2 floods the whole frame with light

density.doc: how many unseen occluders stand between the fire and the scene (2–9) — how broken up the light is

warmth.doc: colour temperature — 0 is a pale gas flame, 1 is deep orange-red wood fire

hue.doc: flame hue — amber by default; the whole ramp swings off it

x.doc: fire position x — default is just off the left edge so only the spill enters

y.doc: fire position y — default is low, on the ground

style.doc: aesthetic — hearth: amber wood fire falling off to deep red, soft penumbrae · forge: near-white core, hard shadows and cold indigo fill in the darks · candle: small, intimate, tight fast falloff to near-black · photometric: the wash resolved into quantised iso-lux contour bands with lux callouts, a lighting plot rather than a room · woodcut: hard three-tone posterisation with a chisel grain, no gradient anywhere

act.doc: multi-minute programme — burn: a steady fire · flare_up: it periodically catches and surges, throw and output swelling together · dying: it sinks toward embers over minutes until someone feeds it and it builds back

seed.doc: occluder placement, pivot rates, gutter phases (int)
